function: Joint design of BS common and private beamformers, rate-splitting coefficients and STAR-RIS phase shifts by TD3 DRL, maximizing sum secrecy rate against eavesdroppers (p. 5-8).
system: Downlink RSMA, BS ULA M=4, K=2 users (outdoor far-field, indoor near-field) with 4 antennas, J=2 eavesdroppers, STAR-RIS UPA 16x2, amplitudes beta_t+beta_r=1, 28 GHz (p. 3-4, 9).
method: TD3 actor-critic DRL (twin critics, delayed policy updates); state is channels, action is beamformers, rate split and RIS phases; reward is secrecy rate minus penalties (p. 6-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: far-field Saleh-Valenzuela BS-RIS channel, near-field RIS-indoor channel from antenna distances, eavesdropper CSI with norm-bounded error; no dataset, online RL interaction (p. 3-5, 9).
test_conditions: Agent trained and evaluated in one simulated scenario; sweeps of Pmax 5-35 dBm, RIS elements 32-80, CEE -30 to 10 dB; no unseen scenario (p. 9-11).
baselines: Learned: DDPG [38], SAC [39] (p. 11); RandomRIS and NoRIS references (p. 10); NOMA and SDMA access variants of the same TD3 scheme (p. 10).
metrics: Sum secrecy rate versus Pmax, number of RIS elements and CEE; average reward convergence; eavesdropper achievable rate; user rates (p. 9-11).
complexity: Order O(Neps T (2MKMk + Mparam)) stated analytically; no FLOPs, parameter count or runtime reported (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 3: "we adopt the Saleh-Valenzuela (SV) channel model, which" for the BS-RIS link; custom Saleh-Valenzuela and distance-based near-field models, with no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "elements {32, 48, 64, 80}." is a sweep of the RIS size, with Pmax and CEE also swept (p. 11); the action dimension depends on N (p. 6), and no scenario unseen in training is tested.
q3_support: p. 11: "DDPG [38] and SAC [39] algorithms to solve the problem," compared by sum secrecy rate (Fig. 9, 10); p. 10: "without optimal passive phase shift (RandomRIS w" RSMA, and NoRIS, as non-learned references.
q4_support: p. 9: "the overall complexity of the proposed algorithm can" be expressed as O(Neps T (2MKMk + Mparam)); the order of complexity is given, with no FLOPs or runtime.
q5_support: p. 9: "For the simulation experiments, we consider a single-cell" scenario simulated by the authors; no code or data link is given, and no public or measured dataset is used.
notes: STAR-RIS with beta_t+beta_r=1 (p. 4). Secrecy-rate objective, but the learned function is beamforming and RIS phase design, so area 3. The paper does not say how the beamformers are obtained in RandomRIS and NoRIS; a random RIS configuration counts as non-learned for q3, which the reviewer may confirm.
